messages:
maria.chen: Quick sync — we need to decide sequencing heuristics for the next model onboard sprint. A couple of strong customer asks (Acme + Nova) for llama2-70b embeddings and a smaller Mistral variant for chat. Thinking RICE + a catalog signal weight for active customers. Any objections to blending heuristics?
alex.liu: No objections. My worry: RICE often upweights launches that are high impact but expensive to operate (high R). We should include an operational cost multiplier or explicit latency SLO hit check.
benji.park: Agree with Alex. Also add a compatibility check with current quantized runtime. Some models (70b fp16) don't hit our cheap-quant path and blow costs.
priya.ram: From customer-ops: Acme is willing to pay for dedicated capacity short-term but wants embeddings in prod in 4 weeks. Nova is lower $$ but strategic for EU partner. We should capture willingness-to-pay as a separate signal, not just the R in RICE.
kevin.obrien: Suggest a two-track admission: "pay-for" fast lane (customer-backed) and "merit" lane (RICE+ecosystem signal). Merit lane gets run through the normal automated evals & infra-fit checks.
maria.chen: Two-track makes sense. For merit lane, can we propose this scoring function snippet?
maria.chen: ```
# simplified score
R = reach_score (0-10)
I = impact_score (0-10)
C = confidence (0-10)
E = effort_estimate (person-weeks)
customer_signal = active_customer_weight (0-1)
score = ((R*I*C)/max(1,E)) * (1 + customer_signal)
```
benji.park: Love the multiplier for customer_signal. But note numerical scaling will skew picks toward low-effort models with decent R/I. That's okay for quick wins but might block high-value large models.
sophie.martinez: Operational checklist we need before admit: quantization path validated, latency 95th under SLO on dedicated infra, rolling deploy plan (canary + fallback), cost-per-1000-tokens estimate. If any of these fail, push to "blocked" queue.
alex.liu: How do we collect the signals? I can add an automated probe in the onboarding PR template to fetch: perf profile, estimated op cost (based on batch/seq), quantization compatibility tag, and customer requests list.
priya.ram: We should also add a "customer urgency" field: "pilot", "ready-prod", "exploratory". That helps prioritize when customer_signal > 0.
kevin.obrien: For the sprint, propose slots: 2 paid-backlog slots (fast lane), 1 merit medium slot, 1 exploratory small slot. That keeps cadence predictable.
maria.chen: Drafted sprint entry criteria in the PR template. Putting it here so eng/product can poke:
maria.chen: ```
Entry criteria:
- performance profile uploaded (latency/cost for 16/32 tokens)
- quantization path validated (yes/no)
- owner assigned + rollout plan
- customer_signal value + urgency
- automated evals: nlu, hallucination, safety smoke tests
```
benji.park: Minor tweak: require a note if model will drop into fallback pool with a cheaper variant (ex: llama2-70b -> 13B fallback) so runtime can stage routing.
sophie.martinez: Agree. Add "fallback_variants" to the template.
onboard-bot: New onboarding PR created: #onboard-728 — includes perf CSV, quant tag=maybe, fallback_variants=[llama2-13b], requested_by=Acme (paid). Status: review needed.
alex.liu: I'll take a look at #onboard-728. If quant tag=maybe we need a small exploration spike to validate 4-bit/awq path.
priya.ram: Customer Acme confirms they'll sign a 3-month reserved capacity once we validate latency. That should move them into paid lane.
kevin.obrien: OK — plan for this week: 
- Alex: perf/quant spike (2d)
- Benji: cost estimate + fallback config (1d)
- Sophie: rollout + canary plan (1d)
- Priya: finalize contract details with Acme (2d)
maria.chen: Thanks. One more debate: prefer sequencing by pure score or by diversity? If we always pick low-effort wins we risk catalog narrowness (only smaller models). Any thoughts on forcing diversity token?
benji.park: I'd add a diversity penalty to the score when the catalog already has >1 similar variant in the same size class. Simple heuristic: diversity_factor = 0.8 if similar exists, else 1.0.
alex.liu: Or treat diversity as an explicit constraint: allocate 1 slot per size-class per sprint. Simpler.
maria.chen: Let's try Alex's constraint for 2 sprints then evaluate. If it stalls the backlog we'll relax it. I'll update the template and post a short doc in the product wiki with these heuristics.
priya.ram: Can we also track outcomes post-onboard? Key metrics: customers_on_prod, cost_delta, latency_change, quality_regression_rate. If a model fails these, we deprecate fast.
sophie.martinez: I'll add those metrics to the rollout checklist.
maria.chen: Great. If no other blockers I'll land the template and we can run the first sprint triage tomorrow 10am.
kevin.obrien: :thumbsup:
alex.liu: 👍
benji.park: I'll block some time for the quant spike.
priya.ram: Noted and coordinating with Acme.
onboard-bot: Reminder: sprint triage meeting scheduled: 2023-11-14T10:00:00Z. Threads linked: #onboard-728."
